issues.legal_issue: The compensation for a plot with some road frontage near more valuable comparable land should reflect both its proximity to that land and its inferior advantages.
material_facts: The acquired plot abutted a less important narrow road and was near land valued in an earlier acquisition judgment at an average rate of Rs. 1,000 per cent.
The comparable land was more advantageously situated, surrounded by roads, and suitable as a commercial building site.
The acquired plot had a slope and no buildings, but it had road access and was not far from the comparable land.
issues.conclusion: The compensation for this plot was enhanced to Rs. 500 per cent.
issues.legal_principle: In fixing market value in a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, a court may use a nearby acquisition judgment as comparable evidence but must account for differences in location and advantages. The court considered the District Court judgment in Exhibit P-7, concerning nearby land acquired shortly afterward, and the High Court judgment in A.S. No. 537 of 1961 concerning adjoining land; it did not treat the more advantageous comparable land as identical to the acquired plot.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and plot_has_road_access and plot_is_near_comparable_land and plot_is_less_advantageous_than_comparable_land

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.plot_has_road_access: The acquired plot abuts a road.
predicates.plot_is_near_comparable_land: The acquired plot is near land whose value is supported by comparable acquisition evidence.
predicates.plot_is_less_advantageous_than_comparabl: The acquired plot has fewer advantages than the comparable land, such as less important road access or a slope.
predicates.compensation_for_plot_set_by_adjusting_c: The compensation for the plot is set by adjusting the comparable value to account for differences between the plots.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a plot with road access near more advantageous comparable land, the comparable value is adjusted for the differences between the plots.

issues.legal_issue: A steep plot without road frontage that would require substantial levelling and terracing does not warrant increased compensation merely because it is contiguous to a more accessible plot.
material_facts: The plot measured 255 cents and was contiguous to the plot for which compensation was enhanced.
It had no road frontage and formed part of a hillside with an average slope of 1 in 6 and a level difference of about 70 feet between its sides.
Use for houses would require considerable levelling and terracing.
issues.conclusion: The existing compensation of Rs. 250 per cent was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: In determining market value in a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, relevant differences in access, terrain, and the cost of making land usable must be considered; contiguity alone does not make two plots equivalent. The court distinguished the plot from the more accessible land considered in the District Court judgment in Exhibit P-7 and the adjoining-land judgment in A.S. No. 537 of 1961.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and plot_lacks_road_frontage and plot_has_steep_slope and making_plot_usable_requires_substantial_work

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.plot_lacks_road_frontage: The acquired plot does not abut a road.
predicates.plot_has_steep_slope: The acquired plot has a substantial slope.
predicates.making_plot_usable_requires_substantial_: Using the plot for its relevant potential use requires substantial levelling, terracing, or similar work.
predicates.existing_compensation_for_plot_is_not_in: The compensation already awarded for the plot is left unchanged.

issues.definition: When a plot in a compensation appeal lacks road frontage, is steep, and requires substantial work to use, its existing compensation is not increased on the basis of a more accessible neighbouring plot.

issues.legal_issue: A level plot abutting a major road may be compensated at the rate supported by comparable land with similar advantages.
material_facts: The acquired plot measured 45 cents, was more or less level, and abutted the main Kottayam-Kumili road.
The court considered the average rate awarded for comparable land in Exhibit P-7.
issues.conclusion: The compensation for the plot was enhanced by a further Rs. 250 per cent.
issues.legal_principle: In fixing market value in a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, comparable land may guide compensation where the acquired plot shares material advantages such as level terrain and major-road frontage. The court relied on the District Court judgment in Exhibit P-7 and its average valuation of the land there; it also referred to the High Court judgment in A.S. No. 537 of 1961 concerning adjoining land and road frontage.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and plot_is_level and plot_abuts_major_road and comparable_land_supports_same_value

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.plot_is_level: The acquired plot is substantially level.
predicates.plot_abuts_major_road: The acquired plot abuts a major road.
predicates.comparable_land_supports_same_value: Comparable land with similar material advantages supports the value used for the acquired plot.
predicates.compensation_for_plot_is_enhanced_to_com: The compensation for the plot is increased to the rate supported by comparable land.

issues.definition: When a plot in a compensation appeal is level, abuts a major road, and comparable land supports the same value, its compensation is enhanced to the comparable rate.
